title: LongSpike: Fractional-Order State Space Modeling for Efficient Long-Memory Learning
claim: A standard encoder-block-decoder stack gains long-memory temporal modeling by swapping first-order state transitions for a fractional-order state-space module.
layout: 3 zoomed regions, left-to-right, dashed zoom lines linking architecture to block details
description: On the left is a vertical architecture stack: Encoder at the bottom, then a Pre-Norm layer and a red-titled LongSpike Block repeated for N layers, and Pooling and Linear Projection in a dashed decoder box, with an Output Head at the top. Dashed lines zoom from this stack into a large dashed panel. The left half of that panel shows the LongSpike Block as three time steps (x, h, y) inside a shaded blue box. Curved dash-dot arrows connect each hidden state to many earlier states, showing long memory. Red spiking-neuron waveform icons sit on top. The right half shows the Baseline SpikingSSM Block, where each hidden state connects only to its immediate neighbor. A dark arrow points from the LongSpike block to a callout box with the f-SSM equations. The A, B and C labels are in pastel colors.
caption: Overview of the LongSpike architecture. Compared with the baseline SpikingSSM [ref], LongSpike incorporates fractional-order state-space dynamics into spiking neurons via an f-SSM module, enabling enhanced temporal modeling with efficient parallel computation.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are well-regarded for their biological plausibility and energy efficiency in processing sequential data. However, dominant SNN architectures typically rely on first-order Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) to govern neuronal state transitions. This first-order formulation induces an exponential-decay memory bias, which can be less suited to representing heavy-tailed temporal dependencies in long-sequence tasks. In this work, we propose LongSpike , a novel SNN framework that integrates fractional-order State-Space Modeling ( f -SSM ) from control theory into the spiking domain. By extending traditional integer-order SSMs to the fractional-calculus regime, LongSpike enables the hierarchical integration of neuronal dynamics with long-memory kernels. To mitigate the computational overhead and parallelization challenges typically associated with fractional operators, we leverage a state-space formulation that supports efficient, parallel training. Empirical evaluations on challenging benchmarks, including Long Range Arena (LRA), large-scale WikiText-103, and Speech Commands, demonstrate that LongSpike outperforms state-of-the-art SNNs in accuracy while preserving sparse synaptic computation.
